newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to charge eight politicians for graft.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to charge eight politicians for graft.

text.p: Eight South Korean politicians, including the mayor of the city of Pusan, will be charged with bribery in a scandal surrounding the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co, the chief prosecutor said on Thursday.
Shim Je-ryoon told reporters the eight were among 33 politicians named by Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo as having accepted money from him.
Mayor Moon Jung-soo of Pusan, South Korea's second largest city, will be charged with accepting kickbacks of 200 million won ($224,000), Shim said.
Among the others are two serving lawmakers and five former members of the National Assembly from both the ruling New Korea Party and opposition parties, he said.

Hanbo founder Chung is now on trial along with 10 other people on charges of bribing politicians and bankers to secure credit for the group's steelmaking flagship, which collapsed in January under debts of five trillion won.
On Wednesday, a presidential Blue House official said 70 high-level officials were under investigation for corruption. ($1=890 won)
